# Microsoft Azure MachineLearning management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Machine Learning is a fully managed cloud service that enables you to easily build, deploy, and share predictive analytics solutions.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Machine Learning resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure MachineLearning management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.MachineLearning
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html)..

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

decisions.reason: The obsolete misspelled extension and virtual hook are both implemented outside Generated; the former guards the client and delegates, and the latter validates the ID and creates the resource. The compatibility-shim pattern describes the retained obsolete API, without relying on comments to prove its history.

The second obsolete misspelled accessor and its matching virtual hook have concrete delegation and resource-construction bodies outside Generated. The Obsolete annotations, rather than the historical assertions in comments, support the compatibility characterization.

The active CodeGenSuppress and the virtual resource factory support a handwritten accessor, but bound-resource-operation-overload describes forwarding operations on a stored resource, not construction from a supplied ID. Comments alone do not prove any specific generator limitation.

finding.subtype: Suppressed mockable resource accessor implemented by hand
finding.explanation: A CodeGenSuppress annotation targets the ResourceIdentifier overload, and the replacement virtual accessor validates the supplied ID and constructs a MachineLearningOutboundRuleBasicResource from Client and id.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The explicit suppression and implementation occur in a Customized partial class outside Generated; an accessor with the same general shape could plausibly be generated, without establishing why this one was suppressed.

decisions.reason: The sync and async AddTag bodies are explicit Customized public methods forwarding the bound tag resource, corresponding Get method, key and value. The proposed pattern describes reusable tag-method wrappers, not the uncaptured helper implementation.
The separate SetTags sync/async pair is implemented outside Generated and passes the supplied dictionary to shared helpers. The finding correctly limits its claim to the visible forwarding behavior.
Both RemoveTag methods have handwritten forwarding expressions for the bound tag resource and key. Actual mutation mechanics remain outside the capture, as the proposal acknowledges.
The endpoint resource independently implements AddTag and AddTagAsync with explicit helper calls outside Generated. It is a distinct resource instance of the same reusable tag-wrapper shape.
The endpoint SetTags pair forwards the caller dictionary and respective Get method to shared helpers. Its bodies and citations are concrete, and no uncaptured helper behavior is asserted.
The endpoint RemoveTag pair supplies the bound tag resource, Get method and key in Customized source; the proposal correctly does not infer the helper's internal service behavior.

The one-line factory is handwritten and cites the right symbol, but bound-resource-operation-overload describes a bound operation forwarded to another method. Here the behavior is construction of a scoped child collection.

finding.handwrittenRationale: The concrete child-collection factory is implemented in a Customized partial resource outside Generated; its construction shape is plausibly generatable.

decisions.reason: The two explicit methods obtain the collection bound to the code container and forward version and cancellation to Get/GetAsync. These are handwritten convenience operations rather than independently implemented REST calls.

Both hidden code-version GetAll signatures supply two nulls to the wider overload; no local pagination loop is claimed. The legacy-overload-compatibility pattern fits the hidden overloads, although the historical motive is not independently established by comments.
The component accessor constructs a child collection rather than forwarding an operation on a bound resource; the scoped-subclient-factory catalog pattern better matches the observable behavior.

decisions.reason: The component-version sync/async accessors use the bound collection and forward version plus cancellation. The ForwardsClientCalls attributes do not negate the visible handwritten method bodies outside Generated.
The hidden component-version list overloads each insert a null argument before skip while forwarding the other arguments; the proposal does not misidentify them as custom paging loops.

A public location-only constructor with a base(location) initializer is a concrete model API addition in Customized source. Its empty body does not make the constructor empty scaffolding; the proposal correctly treats the generated-constructor history in comments as unverified.

decisions.reason: The data container's sync/async accessors forward a version and cancellation through a collection bound to Client and Id. This separate convenience behavior is implemented outside Generated.

The options-taking list methods explicitly unpack seven nullable properties into flattened sync and async overloads. The catalog's convenience-options-unpacking pattern matches exactly and no pager implementation is attributed to these overloads.

The optional sync overload reorders top and skip into the handwritten pager, but it is not annotated hidden or obsolete; the legacy-overload-compatibility catalog description does not establish a legacy API. A parameter-reorder pattern records the observable shape without inferring history.

limitations: Coverage is partial: all 15 captures were read, from 1804 eligible and 1901 discovered files. The 198 explicitly budget-skipped paths were read as inventory only, not source; they include tag helpers, options classes, model factories, serialization, resource and operation implementations.

All scanner kinds are unknown. Handwritten assessment relies on explicit implementations in src/Customized outside Generated without generation headers, under the embedded .NET guideline, not the unknown label itself.

All three complete generation contexts were read. They do not establish old GA API history, current decorator limitations, helper implementations, generated counterparts or runtime behavior; source comments asserting those remain qualified.

Guard and ValidateResourceId calls are observed, not independent proof of their internal exception behavior. Each obsolete extension and matching mock hook are counted together, and the outbound accessor suppression is coupled to its replacement. No uncaptured matching extension is counted.

Six tag-operation pairs only forward a bound tag resource, Get/GetAsync callback and arguments to an uncaptured helper. Mutation, readback, retries, null checking and wire behavior inside that helper are not established.

The two full pagers derive tokens from response NextLink, using AbsoluteUri for absolute links and OriginalString otherwise. Their callback still calls new Uri(nextLink) without an explicit relative-kind argument, so successful relative-link traversal is not asserted. Page-size hints are ignored in these callbacks.

Paging projection, diagnostics and continuation handling are grouped within each pager; thin list overloads are convenience adaptations, not separate paging algorithms. ArmOperation-returning references do not establish a handwritten LRO here.

Generator addressability is plausible API/pager/member shaping, not proven existing support, and no compatibility, sealing or service-success assertion is based only on comments. No oversized tool-output spool was opened.

AI-reviewed judgments on 15 captured Customized files only, not a verified or exhaustive SDK inventory. Coverage reports 15 captures out of 1804 eligible files and 198 explicitly skipped candidate paths; those names do not reveal their contents or establish absence of other customizations.

No generated counterpart, history, tests, or implementation of MachineLearningTagOperationHelpers is supplied. Comments about former API shapes, generator limitations and compatibility motives are not independent proof; those causal claims and actual helper behavior remain unverified.

The captured paging methods show handwritten implementations outside Generated, but supplied evidence does not establish why generated alternatives were unsuitable, nor measured generator support for any proposed pattern.
